children: Slovakia sold €2.5 billion ($2.85 billion) worth of 10-year bonds on international markets, in its second and final syndicated benchmark offering of this year, national debt agency Ardal said late on Wednesday.
Demand exceeded €4.2 billion, down from over €8 billion in bids received in a syndicated 20-year bond offer in February.
Ardal also ran a foreign debt offering with a 700 million Swiss franc ($900 million) sale of three bonds in May.
The new offering was priced at 77 basis points over mid-swaps, Ardal said. Deutsche Bank, HSBC, JPMorgan and Erste Group Bank's Slovenska Sporitelna were joint bookrunners.

Slovakia raised €2 billion from its first syndicated bond sale earlier this year, en route to meeting gross issuance plans of around €10 billion in 2026 as it tackles a budget deficit running above the European Union ceiling.
